newsitem.title: USA: New U.S. power group to focus on electric reform.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. power group to focus on electric reform.

text.p: Two power producer groups announced Tuesday they had joined to form the Electric Power Supply Association, forging a single voice for independent power producers to push for opening all U.S. electricity markets to competition.

The new group, merging the Electric Generation Association and the National Independent Energy Producers, planned to lobby Congress to pass "legislation to bring the benefits of competition to all consumers by a date certain," Steven Burton, senior vice president of Sithe Energies Inc and chairman of the association, said at a news conference.
The Electric Power Supply Association, starting with a budget of $2 million, planned to focus on opening electricity markets nationally but would support affiliates working on the state level.
It said it would push for the federal government to make states offer all homes, offices and industry freedom to choose their power suppliers by the beginning of 2003.
It supported allowing utilities to recoup the costs of investments which would become unprofitable in the new market.
It also backed the development of independent system operators to handle all transmission on regional power grids.

The new association would also press for legislation and regulations which would make old and new power plants have to meet the same pollution standards, measures which natural gas producers have long advocated.

The Electric Generation Association, which largely represented independent power affiliates of utilities, and National Independent Energy Producers, which represented small power producers, came together because their differences had "basically vanished" over the last few years, Burton said.
Jeanine Hull, vice president of LG&E Power, who will be heading the group's lobbying efforts, predicted that Congress would pass sweeping electricity legislation within the next two or three years.
She said several groups were talking about forming a larger coalition to press for open markets but were not yet ready to come out.
